---
title: "Crawling etiquette"
---

Skemman is run by the National and University Library of Iceland for the Icelandic
universities. It is a public service, not a CDN, and it should be treated accordingly.

## What robots.txt asks for

[skemman.is/robots.txt](https://skemman.is/robots.txt) states two things that matter here:

```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /simple-search
...
Crawl-delay: 30
```

**A 30-second delay between requests.** `request_delay_seconds` in
`config/collections.yaml` defaults to 30 for that reason. Lowering it is a decision to
ignore what the server asked for. If you have a reason — a conversation with the library,
a tiny harvest — that is yours to make, but make it deliberately.

**`/simple-search` is disallowed.** Use `oai-pmh` for listing records.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `simple-search` goes against robots.txt

Skemman is a DSpace repository and exposes **OAI-PMH** at
[`/oai/request`](https://skemman.is/oai/request?verb=Identify) — the standard interface for
listing records out of a repository, designed for exactly this, and not disallowed. The
`oai-pmh` command uses this endpoint.

`/handle/` and `/bitstream/`, which `metadata-load` and `titlepage-load` use, are not
disallowed.
:::

## What this tool does

**One request at a time.** No concurrency, no connection pools. Requests are serialized.

**The delay applies only to network fetches.** A thesis served from cache costs nothing and
waits for nothing, so a re-run over cached material is instant regardless of the delay.

**An identifiable user agent.** Set `user_agent` in `config/collections.yaml` with a real
contact address. A contactable crawler gets an email when something is wrong; an anonymous
one gets blocked.

**Closed files are never requested.** `files-index` reads the access status off the item
page, and anything not marked `Opinn` is skipped without a request. In a typical university
collection that is several hundred requests never made.

**Failures are not retried blindly.** A file that answers 403, 404 or a login page is
recorded as permanently unavailable and skipped from then on. Only transient failures are
tried again.

## What it will not do

No logins, no session tokens, no cookies. No bypassing embargoes: a thesis under embargo
stays under embargo. No CAPTCHA solving, no user-agent rotation, no anti-bot evasion.

## If you lower the delay

At 30 seconds a thousand theses take about eight hours. That is the number robots.txt
implies, and for a one-off harvest it is worth simply letting it run overnight.

If you do lower it, lower it once, for a known-size job, having thought about who is on the
other end. And put a real address in `user_agent` first, so they can reach you rather than
just block you.
